inputs.text: Organizers estimate that 8 million people took part in more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states—about one million more than in October. There’s no official count, so it’s an estimate, not a mandate. But that doesn’t make the protest meaningless: elections alone don’t ensure that people—especially those already shut out of political power—are heard. Invoking “law and tradition” to quiet dissent often serves those who benefit from the status quo. Peaceful protest is one way ordinary people can demand accountability between elections, and those in power shouldn’t confuse holding office with having everyone’s consent.
